study_notes.title: Start here: staff workflow
study_notes.text: Record the ticket, symptom, Windows version and recent changes. Begin with read-only checks. Choose one specific repair, explain its impact, record the result and retest the symptom. Keep logs with the ticket after reviewing device/user details. There is no universal run-all command that fixes every PC. The terminal toolkit asks for YES on state-changing operations and does not reboot automatically.

study_notes.title: Registry basics
study_notes.text: Win+R opens Run; regedit opens Registry Editor. Keys contain subkeys and typed values. HKLM contains machine settings; HKCU the executing user; HKCR merged classes/file associations; HKU loaded profiles; HKCC current hardware configuration. REG_SZ is text, REG_DWORD a 32-bit number, REG_BINARY bytes, REG_EXPAND_SZ text with expandable variables. Export the specific key before an authorized edit. A .reg export is a partial backup, not system recovery. Import merges values and does not remove later additions. GUI workflow: select key, Export, then inspect/create/edit only the required values. Wallpaper edits may not refresh the desktop immediately. Use supported policy/settings for Windows Update and file associations; no universal disable-updates registry tweak is provided.

study_notes.title: BSOD triage
study_notes.text: Record stop code, time, driver name and recent changes. Preserve dump files and correlate System logs. Stop codes suggest areas to investigate, not certain causes. Kernel-Power 41 alone does not establish a cause. Check storage health, RAM, cooling and manufacturer-approved drivers. Back up data before disk repairs; protect a failing disk before intensive scans. CHKDSK cannot physically repair broken hardware. Memory tests and some disk operations require a reboot. Review recent updates and overclocking. Reinstallation is a last resort after preserving data. The source bash/Copy labels are formatting artifacts; SFC and CHKDSK are Windows commands.

study_notes.title: Windows keys and official activation
study_notes.text: Use the console licensing commands in Licensing and activation. Firmware keys can be absent; keys must match the licensed edition. Product keys in the supplied source were redacted. Never include recovered keys in shared logs. The source also describes remote download-and-execute activation scripts: these remain unreviewed source text only and have no command button. Use official activation or your organization's licensed activation method. Do not change execution policy or Script Host merely to bypass an organization policy.

study_notes.title: PowerShell source corrections
study_notes.text: Use "$($city.Length)" for property expansion inside strings. "$city.length" is not equivalent in PowerShell 5.1. The supplied $msg = "Hello World") has an unmatched closing parenthesis. Syntax diagrams such as <string> and [-Name] are documentation, not paste-ready commands. Install-WUUpdates is not a built-in cmdlet; identify its supplying module before considering it. Get-WmiObject/Get-EventLog are Windows PowerShell legacy commands; prefer CIM/Get-WinEvent in PowerShell 7. Help -ShowWindow is graphical. The source PowerShell 7.3 links are historical version-pinned references. Date formats, operators and sample functions are learning material, not repairs.

study_notes.title: Keyboard layouts and Windows-key shortcuts
study_notes.text: British en-GB: 00000809. US en-US: 00000409. Danish da-DK: 00000406. German Germany de-DE: 00000407. These are standard layouts, not variants such as US International or Swiss German. Win+Space switches installed layouts; Win+I opens Settings, then Time & language > Language & region > Language options > Keyboards. Win+X opens administrative shortcuts; Win+R opens Run. Physical key labels do not change with the selected layout. Get-WinUserLanguageList inspects the current user; preserve existing language lists when adding a layout. Your supplied images depict Danish, US and British. German uses QWERTZ, swaps Y/Z, and includes Ä Ö Ü ß. Cp / roo was unclear and is retained without interpretation.

study_notes.title: God Mode and Control Panel
study_notes.text: God Mode is a graphical index of existing Control Panel tasks, not an elevated repair mode or a complete list of every Windows setting. Some tasks vary by Windows build and edition. GUI references are retained for the manual; the terminal menu does not launch them. sysdm.cpl opens System Properties and computer-name/domain settings, not Add Hardware. hdwwiz.exe opens the Add Hardware wizard; hdwwiz.cpl usually opens Device Manager. Several original applets belong to older Windows versions and are marked legacy.

study_notes.title: Group Policy, backups and rollback
study_notes.text: Use gpresult to inspect effective policy before changing settings. Managed domain/MDM policy can override local changes. gpupdate refreshes policy; it does not remove restrictive settings. Registry and firewall toolkit changes save the previous selected values, with restore actions in the same menu. Feature changes use NoRestart; reboot manually when required. A backup of one registry value or firewall profile is not a complete configuration backup. Account creation and memberships require explicit technician choices; retain a working admin account.

study_notes.title: Windows Server and domain scope
study_notes.text: Server/AD/DNS/DHCP tools require the installed role or RSAT modules plus authorized connectivity. Server Core may lack graphical tools. Windows Sandbox does not reproduce a domain or every Windows Server role. Placeholders such as yourdomain.local need the actual authorized lab target. No production domain query was executed during this rebuild.

study_notes.title: PowerShell setup: scripts are disabled
study_notes.text: The saved toolkit cannot start when the effective execution policy blocks scripts. Inspect policy scopes before choosing the approved workflow.
